title: How Many Ones?

concept.title: Count position by position
body: How many times does the digit `1` appear when you write down all the numbers from 1 to `n`? For `n = 13` the numbers are 1, 2, ..., 9, 10, 11, 12, 13 and the digit appears in 1, 10, 11 (twice), 12 and 13: six times. For `n = 10^17` you cannot write the numbers down.

The trick is to ask a different question: for each **position** (units, tens, hundreds, ...) how many numbers have a `1` there? Let `factor` be 1, 10, 100, ... for the position being looked at, and split `n` around it:

list: `high` = the digits to the left of the position (`n / (factor * 10)`)
`current` = the digit at the position (`n / factor % 10`)
`low` = the digits to the right (`n % factor`)

body: Complete cycles: for every value of `high` below its current value there are `factor` numbers with a 1 at this position, so `high * factor` numbers. The last, partial cycle depends on `current`: if `current` is 0 there are no more; if it is 1 there are `low + 1` more (the numbers up to `n` itself); if it is bigger than 1 the whole cycle of `factor` numbers fits.

body.code:
if current == 0:   count += high * factor
elif current == 1: count += high * factor + low + 1
else:              count += (high + 1) * factor

body: Check it on `n = 13`. Units position (`factor = 1`): `high = 1`, `current = 3`, `low = 0`; since `current > 1` the count is `(1 + 1) * 1 = 2` (the numbers 1 and 11). Tens position (`factor = 10`): `high = 0`, `current = 1`, `low = 3`; the count is `0 * 10 + 3 + 1 = 4` (the numbers 10, 11, 12 and 13). Together 6, as counted by hand.
Adding this over all positions needs one round per digit of `n`: 18 rounds instead of 10^17.

statement: Given `n`, count how many times the digit `1` appears in the decimal notation of all integers from 1 to `n`.
outputFormat: The number of times the digit 1 appears.
hints: Do not go through the numbers. Count for each position (units, tens, ...) separately.
For the position with value `factor`: `high = n / (factor * 10)`, `current = (n / factor) % 10`, `low = n % factor`.
Add `high * factor` if current is 0, `high * factor + low + 1` if it is 1, and `(high + 1) * factor` if it is larger. Move on with `factor *= 10`.

explanation: Each digit position is counted on its own. The full cycles to the left of the position contribute `high * factor` numbers with a 1 there, and the partial cycle contributes depending on the digit at that position. With `n` up to 10^17, `factor * 10` never exceeds 10^18, so no overflow occurs.
solution.complexity: Time O(number of digits of n), space O(1).

code.python:
n = int(input())

count = 0
factor = 1
while factor <= n:
    high = n // (factor * 10)
    current = n // factor % 10
    low = n % factor
    if current == 0:
        count += high * factor
    elif current == 1:
        count += high * factor + low + 1
    else:
        count += (high + 1) * factor
    factor *= 10
print(count)
